checks: No eclipse at 4 of 20 covered epochs where the 13.15231 d period predicts one (each under half the typical depth, > 5 sigma below it). The period is probably wrong - the dips seen may be separate eclipses of a longer-period system.
writeup: TIC 313485023 is a candidate eclipsing binary star identified through automated analysis of TESS photometry data. The system shows a primary eclipse with a depth of 1.28% and an orbital period of 13.152313 days. A secondary eclipse was detected at 5.7 sigma significance. The star does not appear in six checked variable-star catalogs, making it a previously uncatalogued candidate. Pixel-level image analysis confirms the signal with a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 30.3, though the centroid offset of 2.5 arcsec from the target warrants further investigation. One data quality metric indicates that alternating eclipses differ significantly in depth, which is consistent with the corrected period reported here rather than the initial BLS finding.
